title: Scale-covariant liquid in nonlocal high Tc strange metals
abstract: Experiments in recent years on high $T_c$ superconductors find a puzzling nodal scale-covariant self-energy with an exponent varying continuously with doping. We propose a mechanism: nonlocality induced by poorly screened effective repulsions $V_α(r) \sim 1/r^α$, where a continuously doping-dependent exponent $1 \le α\le 3$ naturally interpolates between the Mott insulating and Fermi liquid limits. We develop a phenomenology of hydrodynamic screening, finding a scale-covariant quasiparticle decay rate $Γ(ω,T) \propto T^γ Φ(ω/T)$ in energy $ω$ and temperature $T$, with $γ= 2-\frac{1}α$ for nonlocal $ 1 < α< 2$. Our results naturally capture the optimally doped to overdoped regimes, whereas the underdoped regime is qualitatively distinct. In our theory, spectroscopy-fitted exponents directly probe the charged fluid's effective spatial nonlocality. Nonlocality shows that quantum criticality is not necessary to explain scale-covariant phenomena.
summary: This theoretical work addresses the puzzling normal state of high-Tc superconductors by modeling it using poorly screened, non-local repulsive interactions. The authors derive a scale-covariant quasiparticle decay rate whose exponent depends continuously on doping via an interaction parameter $\alpha$. This framework successfully unifies observations across different doping regimes without requiring quantum criticality.
main_problem: To develop a theory explaining the scale-covariant, doping-dependent normal state of high-$T_c$ strange metals without invoking quantum criticality.
main_result: The authors propose that poorly screened, non-local effective repulsions $V_\alpha(r) \sim 1/r^\alpha$ naturally explain the observed power-law decay rate $\Gamma(\omega, T) \propto T^\gamma$, where $\gamma = 2 - 1/\alpha$.
method: The theory uses a hydrodynamic screening phenomenology and calculates the inelastic quasiparticle decay rate ($\Gamma_{	ext{inel}}$) via diagrammatic techniques within the G0W approximation.
model_or_system: The system is high-$T_c$ superconductors exhibiting strange metal behavior. The model incorporates an interaction potential whose spatial nonlocality is parameterized by a doping-dependent exponent $\alpha$ ($1 \le \alpha \le 3$).
key_observables: Scale-covariant quasiparticle decay rate ($\Gamma(\omega, T)$), quasiparticle residue ($Z_k$), and the effective spatial nonlocality probed by $\alpha(p)$.
important_parameters: Doping level (controlling $\alpha$), temperature $T$, energy $\omega$, and the exponent $\alpha$ itself.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on heuristic assumptions for charge relaxation (continuity law) and approximations concerning momentum transfer ($q \ll k_F$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 proposes a phase diagram showing that optimal and overdoped regimes are captured by $1 \le \alpha \le 2$ using poorly screened repulsions.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem of scale-covariant self-energy in strange metals. It then develops the hydrodynamic screening phenomenology, calculates $\Gamma_{	ext{inel}}$ using linear response theory, and finally derives the scaling relation $\gamma = 2 - 1/\alpha$ to unify different doping regimes.
why_interesting: The focus on nonlocality as an alternative mechanism for anomalous transport properties is highly relevant to understanding strongly correlated electron systems where simple Fermi liquid descriptions fail.
